speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; to begin my evaluation, have these symptoms been present for more than a week?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever (RMSF).

The timeline of fever, headache, and a rash spreading from the wrists/ankles to the trunk, combined with the specific description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area, is highly characteristic of RMSF. I am requesting immediate images of the rash and blood work to confirm the diagnosis.
REQUEST IMAGES: Rash
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Peripheral Blood Smear, Indirect Fluorescent Antibody (IFA) for Rickettsia rickettsii.
